To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the identification of bird songs can be achieved with high accuracy, (ii) the accuracy of the identification is not affected by the number of classes and (iii) the accuracy of identification is improved by using short audio segments instead of complete audio signals.

(1) the performance of the identification procedure is highly dependent on the number of classes; (2) using pulses instead of full audio signals improves the accuracy; (3) using a subset of the most relevant features also improves the accuracy.

the use of pulses as input for the identification procedure improves the identification accuracy of bird songs, and the identification accuracy of the system is not significantly affected by the number of classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an automatic system to identify bird species from their recorded song.

a complete scenario of automatic bird species identification, including the extraction of relevant audio features, the use of machine learning techniques, and the evaluation of the influence of the audio signal characteristics in the identification accuracy.
the development of a system able to automatically identify bird species from their recorded songs in a large number of bird species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the identification of bird species is possible with high accuracy, and it is possible to use short segments of the audio signals to identify bird species with a similar performance as the use of the entire audio signal.
, in general, the identification accuracy is higher when using the pulses instead of the complete signal, and that the identification accuracy decreases when the number of classes increases.
the identification accuracy of bird species is highly dependent on the number of classes, the number of pulses used to identify the species and the audio processing applied to the audio signals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to identify bird species using a dataset of 100 bird species.

the identification accuracy of the system depends strongly on the number of bird species, and that the use of short audio segments (i.e., pulses) instead of the complete audio signal, is a good approach to increase the identification accuracy.
we are able to achieve a 100% of accuracy in the bird species identification task for a dataset of 20 species, with an average accuracy of 98% in the 50 species dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to automatically identify bird species using audio recorded song with a high degree of accuracy.
it is possible to obtain good results in bird species identification using only a short segment of audio signal, even when the number of classes is large.
the bird species identification accuracy is not influenced by the number of classes in the problem, as long as the number of classes is not too high.
